raw_segments.text: This equality, however, between the rent and profit of grass and those of corn, of the
land of which the immediate produce is food for cattle, and of that of which the immediate
produce is food for men, must be understood to take place only through the greater part
of the improved lands of a great country.
In some particular local situations, it is quite otherwise, and the rent and profit of
grass are much superior to what can be made by corn.
